messages:
noah: fleetbot flagged a rising row-remap rate on pool42/card16 — 12 remap events in ~6h + a few Xid 61s. noticed during capacity scan, marking here for triage.

fleetbot: Automated alert: GPU row_remap_count increased to 12 in 6h on pool42/card16. Severity: warning. See /ops/alerts/1948219999

alyssa: @noah can you paste nvml / dmesg snippets? want to confirm ECC vs transient Xid patterns. if its creeping remap we should put it on the watchlist and stop scheduling new long-lived jobs on it.

noah: pasted quick logs below (nvml + dmesg excerpts):
```
NVML RemapCount: 12
XidErrors: 5 (last: 2026-11-10T13:02:11Z)
Card FW: 98.3.1
dmesg:
[Nov10 12:59:22] NVRM: Xid (PCIe) 61 at channel 0
[Nov10 13:01:07] NVRM: page_remap occurred: row_remap=3
[Nov10 13:10:45] NVRM: ECC corrected errors increased on device 16
```

mike: ok not immediate catastrophic but definitely trending. my suggested triage:
1) soft-drain the card during next quiet window (avoid preemptible backfills)
2) run gpu-memcheck (memtest + nvml stress) for 2h with logging
3) if remap_count exceeds 20 or Xid > 10 in 48h, escalate to replacement and schedule hardware swap
assigning INFRA-8721 (tracking ticket).

sophia: adding pool42/card16 to the "watchlist" label and putting a soft cap on new batch allocations. updating autoscaler to prefer other pools.

alyssa: also verify neighboring cards in same chassis — thermal hotspot could cause localized degradation. check pool42/card14 & card15.

noah: quick cluster scan: card14 remap=1, card15 remap=0, card16 remap=12. looks localized to card16. started gpu-memcheck job and attached logs to INFRA-8721.

fleetbot: Action logged: INFRA-8721 created by noah. Suggested SLA: replace within 7 days if remap_count > 25 OR XidErrors > 10 in 48h.

mike: i'll coordinate swap window next Tue 02:00-04:00 UTC. @sophia can you reserve two spare cards in pool42 and pre-stage replacement parts? :thumbsup:

sophia: on it — reserving spares and blocking slot. will reroute traffic and update routing rules before swap. marking this thread "awaiting-swap" until done.

noah: thanks all — monitoring alerts/metrics and will post memcheck results. will escalate sooner if ECC corrected errors spike.
